entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The first major written compilation of Jewish oral traditions (Oral Torah), redacted by Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi (Judah the Prince) around 200 CE. Organized into six "orders" (sedarim) — Zeraim (Seeds/Agriculture), Moed (Festival), Nashim (Women/Marriage), Nezikin (Damages/Civil Law), Kodashim (Holy Things/Sacrifices), and Tohorot (Purities) — containing 63 tractates. The Mishnah preserves centuries of rabbinic legal debate between schools of Hillel and Shammai, establishing the dialectical method of halakhic reasoning that defines all subsequent Jewish legal discourse. It became the foundational text upon which both Talmuds were built.
